parent_company.value: Sika AG, Baar, Switzerland (listed on SIX Swiss Exchange; India operations through Sika India Pvt. Ltd., Kolkata)

product_portfolio.value: Concrete admixtures, structural epoxy adhesives and anchors (Sikadur), repair mortars (SikaTop, Sika MonoTop), waterproofing membranes and liquid systems (Sikalastic, SikaProof), sealants (Sikaflex), industrial and decorative flooring (Sikafloor), roofing and tile-fixing systems

market_coverage.value: Subsidiaries in 103 countries and over 400 factories; ~33,700 employees and CHF 11.2 bn revenue (2025). In India, national dealer coverage with a strong presence in metro infrastructure, industrial and repair contracting

quality_strength_note.value: Datasheet-led brand: every product ships with a full technical data sheet and an India-specific formulation where the climate demands it. Sikadur-31 IN is rated to +40 °C rather than the +30 °C global variant, which is why it holds up on South Indian sites.

contractor_preference.value: First choice for specified structural repair, retrofitting and strengthening work; contractors trust the Sikadur name on tender submissions even where a cheaper local epoxy would pass.

novice_preference.value: Low. Rarely bought by homeowners — sold through project counters and specialist repair dealers rather than hardware shops, and the pack sizes start at 3 kg.

project_vs_retail_cost_note.value: Project-rate supply on a Sika India schedule typically lands 12–18 % under counter rate for orders above ~100 kg; retail counter buyers in Hyderabad and Vijayawada pay the top of the band.

bulk_discount_note.value: 30 kg units carry the best per-kg rate; a further 5–8 % is normal on multi-unit site orders released against a single project code.

dealer_margin_note.value: Roughly 10–15 % on construction-chemical lines, thinner than on cement but supported by higher ticket value per pack.

value.strong: Pan-India, led by metro and industrial corridors

primary_use.value: Structural bonding and epoxy repair in concrete rehabilitation

special_use.value: Segmental bridge adhesives, carbon-fibre plate bonding and metro tunnel segment sealing

product.name: Sika Sikadur-31 IN Structural Epoxy Adhesive

variant_label: 6 kg pre-batched unit (Part A 4 kg + Part B 2 kg)

price.note: Sika publishes no MRP for Sikadur-31 IN. Estimated from Indian distributor quotes of ₹345–425/kg seen on IndiaMART listings in August 2026 (≈ ₹2,070–2,550 for the 6 kg unit); ±10 %. Sika India's own storefront lists a 'Sikadur-31, 6 kg x 2' pack at ₹1,639 but the listing image dates from 2017 and the price is treated as stale.

production_method.value: Factory pre-batched two-component unit; Part A resin and Part B hardener are supplied in the correct proportions for whole-unit site mixing

application_thickness_mm.value: 30 mm maximum per layer; thicker sections built up in successive 30 mm layers once the previous layer has hardened

chemical_resistance.value: Good abrasion and chemical resistance; impermeable to liquids and water vapour

bonding_substrates.value: Concrete, hard natural stone, ceramics, fibre cement, mortar, bricks, blocks and masonry, steel, iron, aluminium, wood, polyester, epoxy and glass

primary_applications.value: Structural bonding of concrete elements, stone, steel and timber; fast-setting repair mortar for corners, edges, holes and voids; rigid joint filling and sealing of non-moving cracks

coverage.value: Approximately 2.0 kg per m² for every 1 mm of layer thickness; a 6 kg unit covers about 3 m² at 1 mm

is_standard.value: ASTM C 881 Type I, Grade 3, Class B+C — no BIS/ISI mark declared for this product

astm_standard.value: ASTM C 881, Type I, Grade 3, Class B+C; strengths tested to ASTM C 579, ASTM C 882, ASTM D 2730, DIN EN 196 and ISO 527

batch_testing.value: All published technical data are laboratory-test values; each pre-batched unit carries a production date and batch code on the pack

application_method.value: Stir Part A briefly, add Part B and mix continuously for at least 3 minutes with a spindle on a slow-speed drill (max. 300 rpm), then decant and mix a further minute; apply with spatula, trowel, notched trowel or gloved hand to both faces to be bonded

surface_preparation.value: Concrete and mortar must be at least 28 days old, sound, clean and dry or matt damp, free from standing water, laitance, efflorescence, oil, grease and loose particles; prepare mechanically by abrasive blasting, needle gunning, scabbling or grinding, and remove all dust by vacuum. Steel to a bright metal finish; wood planed or sanded

application_temperature_range.value: +10 °C to +40 °C for product, ambient air and substrate; the substrate must stay at least 3 °C above dew point

pack_type.value: Pre-batched unit — Part A 4 kg plus Part B 2 kg; also supplied as 3 kg (2 + 1) and 30 kg (20 + 10) units

storage_conditions.value: Store in the original unopened, sealed and undamaged packaging in dry conditions between +5 °C and +40 °C; protect from direct sunlight

warranty_coverage.value: Sika's product data sheet expressly gives no warranty of merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose; cover in practice is limited to replacement of material shown to be defective on manufacture within its shelf life. The user must test suitability for the intended application

short_description: Sikadur-31 IN two-part thixotropic structural epoxy adhesive and repair mortar, 6 kg pre-batched unit. Mix 2:1, 40 min pot life.
long_description:
## What it is

Sikadur-31 IN is Sika's India formulation of its best-known structural epoxy: a solvent-free, moisture-tolerant, thixotropic two-part adhesive and repair mortar based on epoxy resin with special fillers. It is supplied as a factory pre-batched unit — Part A resin and Part B hardener in different colours, so a streak-free grey mix is your own proof that the blend is right. Rated for use between +10 °C and +40 °C, it is built for Indian site temperatures rather than European ones.

## What it's for

Three jobs in one pack. As a structural adhesive it bonds concrete elements, hard natural stone, ceramics, fibre cement, mortar, brick, block and masonry, steel, iron, aluminium, wood, polyester, epoxy and glass. As a fast-setting repair mortar it rebuilds corners, edges, joint arises and fills holes and voids. As a filler it seals rigid joints and non-moving cracks. It is suitable for structural use, indoors and out.

## Key specifications

Mix Part A to Part B at 2:1 by weight and you get roughly 40 minutes of pot life at +30 °C. Mixed density is 1.80 kg/L and the paste is non-sag up to 10 mm on a vertical face, so it stays where you put it overhead. Cured strengths reach 55 MPa in compression and 20 MPa in flexure at seven days, with tensile strength of 8 MPa and a tensile adhesion strength to concrete of 10 MPa — a bond that fails in the concrete, not the glue line. Build up to 30 mm in a single layer. Conformity is declared to ASTM C 881 Type I, Grade 3, Class B+C; no BIS mark is claimed. Shelf life is 12 months.

## Application notes

Concrete must be at least 28 days old, sound, clean, and dry or matt damp — never under standing water. Prepare mechanically by blasting, scabbling or grinding to an open gripping profile and vacuum off all dust; take steel to bright metal. Mix Part A briefly, add Part B, and mix at most 300 rpm for three minutes plus a further minute after decanting. Apply to both faces with a spatula or trowel. Keep the substrate 3 °C above dew point and support heavy components until cure. Consumption is about 2.0 kg/m² per mm of thickness.

## What's in the box

One 6 kg pre-batched unit: Part A resin 4 kg and Part B hardener 2 kg. Also stocked in 3 kg and 30 kg units.
